record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.original_question: Characterize Helly circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs without assuming that the input graph is already a circle graph. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle, and a Helly circle graph has a circle model with pairwise different chords such that every pairwise intersecting subset of chords has a common point. The desired result should list the induced obstructions whose absence is exactly equivalent to being a Helly circle graph.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Characterize Helly circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A circle graph is the intersection graph of a finite family of chords of a circle: vertices correspond to chords, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding chords cross. A circle model of a graph G is such a representation of G by chords (with all chords pairwise distinct). A circle model is said to be Helly if every subfamily of pairwise crossing chords has a point common to all chords of the subfamily. A graph G is called a Helly circle graph if it admits a Helly circle model.

Provide a structural characterization of Helly circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs, valid in the class of all finite simple graphs (i.e., without assuming a priori that the input graph is a circle graph). Concretely, exhibit a family F of finite graphs such that, for every finite simple graph G, the graph G is a Helly circle graph if and only if G contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of F.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search indicates that no forbidden induced subgraph characterization of Helly circle graphs (in the class of all graphs) is currently known. Even the analogous problem for the broader class of circle graphs, and the related problem for Helly circular-arc graphs, remain unresolved in general; partial results exist only in restricted subclasses (e.g., split graphs, chordal graphs, or after assuming the input is a circle/circular-arc graph). The problem therefore appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circle graphs within split graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A structural characterization by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs for the entire class of circle graphs is not known, not even restricted to split graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Even for circle graphs themselves, the global forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization remains unknown, indicating the Helly subcase is also open.

status_evidence.title: Essential obstacles to Helly circular-arc graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Essential obstacles are precisely the minimal forbidden induced circular-arc subgraphs for the class of Helly circular-arc graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related Helly-type characterization problems are studied only relative to the ambient class, with the unrestricted forbidden-subgraph characterization still open.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden Induced Subgraphs of Normal Helly Circular-Arc Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Forbidden induced subgraph characterization for normal Helly circular-arc graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous problems have been resolved only for normal Helly circular-arc graphs, not for Helly circle graphs.
